- * The signedness of a value is relevant when that value is widened. For instance, - * when an {@code int} is widened to a {@code long}, the signedness determines - * whether the value should be sign extended as specified by {@jls 5.1.2}, - * or zero extended as specified by the {@link Integer#toUnsignedLong(int)} method. - *

- * The signedness of a value is used by the {@linkplain Linker linker} to implement - * the calling convention on certain platforms that required the widening of values - * as part of a calling sequence. Outside the linker, signedness is not used by - * the APIs in the {@code java.lang.foreign} package.
